stem: A SaaS company with 22 people spends €18K a month on cards, you would be talking to the founder-CEO, and they announced a Series B in {{month:tom_series_b}}. What total does the scale give, and what do you do?

options.text: 23 out of 25, so you dial today
options.rationale: Funded SaaS scores 5 on industry, 22 people 5, €18K a month 4, a founder 5 and a round announced in {{month:tom_series_b}} 4. That makes 23, and Tom gets a call today.

options.text: 21 out of 25, so you dial this week
options.rationale: A founder who signs off spending scores 5 on access. With that the sum is 23 and the lead goes on today's list.

options.text: 18 out of 25, so you dial this week
options.rationale: A round announced in {{month:tom_series_b}} is a dated event within six months and scores 4. The total is 23.

options.text: 16 out of 25, so you skip it
options.rationale: Nothing here is below the floor. €18K a month is above €10K, and 22 people sit in the 20 to 99 band.

stem: Which of these signals scores 5 on intent?

options.text: The owner announced a second store, opened in {{month:maria_store}}
options.rationale: A dated growth event in the last six months scores 4. It is a good reason to call, but the buyer hasn't asked for one.

options.text: The company filed its annual accounts
options.rationale: Every company files its accounts, and a routine filing scores 2.

options.text: The operations head posted about the tools her team uses
options.rationale: Growth news without a date or a link to spending scores 3 at most.

options.text: The buyer replied to your sequence: "interesting, talk {{today}}?"
options.rationale: A reply or a request for a call in the last week scores 5. Emma's reply is why she is a lead you call today.

stem: Pine Mills distributes food wholesale from one warehouse with 38 people and spends about £22K a month on cards, around €26K. The owner signs off spending, but the accounts are flat and he posts that 'Sage gets me through.' What do you do with this lead?

options.text: Dial today, because the owner is on the phone and the spend is good
options.rationale: The owner and the spend are strong. Flat accounts and no pain put intent at 1, and the total of 19 puts the lead on this week's list.

options.text: Dial this week, because the total is 19 and intent is the weak spot
options.rationale: Wholesale with one site scores 4, 38 people 5, £22K a month 4, the owner 5 and intent 1. That makes 19 and puts the lead on this week's list.

options.text: Skip it, because wholesale isn't one of our segments
options.rationale: Wholesale is a close neighbour of our core segments and scores 4 on industry. Add up all five scores before you decide.

options.text: Skip it, because it is below the card-spend floor
options.rationale: The floor is €10K a month. £22K is about €26K, well above it, and scores 4.

stem: You score a new lead 4 on industry, 4 on size, 3 on card spend, 4 on access to the decision-maker and 3 on intent. What do you do?

options.rationale: The five scores add up to 18. Only 22 or more gets a call today.
A total of 18 is the bottom of the band from 18 to 21. Only a total under 18 is skipped.
The five scores add up to 18, the bottom of the band from 18 to 21, and the lead goes on this week's list.

options.text: Dial first and score it after the call
options.rationale: Scoring after the call is how a rep ends up spending eight minutes on a lead outside the profile.
